extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly: engineers, cartographers, geographers, statisticians, and informed scientific public
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and reviewing geographical maps (cartographic products) with attention to methods, accuracy, usefulness, and aesthetic qualities; also includes methodological criteria for statistical studies of suicide by religion appearing on the same page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness (primary mission of a map)
rubrics_metrics.description: So much for its usefulness, which is the first and principal mission of a map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A map's foremost criterion is practical usefulness: it should serve the engineer in his projects, the geologist in his studies, the tourist on his travels, the soldier on his march, and the emigrant in his search for a home. A map should be judged by how well it fulfills these practical roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (inappreciable error)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the end we have a map of which the error is, in general, inappreciable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should achieve very small errors; accuracy is obtained by combining field reconnaissance with geodetic controls and by incorporating reliable information from other sources (e.g., land-surveys). 'Inappreciable' error is presented as an ideal standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness (time and money)
rubrics_metrics.description: the cost in time and money is comparatively insignificant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective mapping method should produce high-quality results while keeping time and monetary cost comparatively low; cost-efficiency is an explicit evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined surveying methods (methodological completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods in question combine the rapid reconnaissance, the mountain sketch, and the barometrical height upon a precise geodetic basis, incorporating all reliable information attainable from other sources, especially the land-surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred mapping methodology uses a combination of rapid reconnaissance, sketching, barometrical heights tied to a geodetic basis, and incorporation of other reliable sources (itineraries, boundary surveys, geological surveys). Evaluation should consider whether such complementary techniques were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful portrayal and multi-purpose sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: So faithfully may the features of a country be portrayed in this way, that the map of Lake Tahoe ... is sufficient to guide the engineer in his projects, the geologist in his studies, the tourist on his travels, the soldier on his march, and the emigrant in his search for a home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess maps for fidelity to physical features and whether portrayal is sufficiently detailed and reliable for multiple user groups and purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetic and graphic quality
rubrics_metrics.description: As a work of art, graphically delineating the configuration of a district of surpassing beauty and variety of scenery, it will, perhaps, possess greater interest to the ordinary observer than any scientific value of accuracy and completeness could give it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A map should be evaluated for graphic/artistic quality: clear delineation, good use of conventional signs, and the ability to present a comprehensive set of topographical forms in an aesthetically pleasing manner as well as scientifically useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of topographical representation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person were called upon to construct an ideal map which should group together specimens of all types of topographical form and the conventional signs known to the draughtsman, he could hardly derive from his imagination a chart more comprehensive than this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should be judged on how comprehensively they exhibit varied topographic features and standard cartographic conventions; inclusion of diverse terrain types and conventional symbols is a mark of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of proof when studying religion's influence on suicide
rubrics_metrics.description: The first is furnished by the indication of the form of worship to which suicides belong; ... The second is the approximate relation between the number of violent deaths and the predominant form of worship in given countries; and here the most fertile in results are the statistics of the states having inhabitants of various forms of worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating studies of religion and suicide, consider whether authors (a) identify the religion of individual suicides and (b) analyze correlations between violent-death rates and predominant forms of worship, especially using mixed-religion states for comparative leverage. Note that the first type of evidence is often missing in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Within-country comparisons to control social/political confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: But much more correct than this comprehensive comparison is that between the proselytes of different religions in the same country, because then the political and social conditions do not vary, and the due homogeneity of comparative data remains the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer within-country comparisons (comparing adherents of different faiths in the same polity) to control for political, social, and environmental confounders. This is recommended as a methodological standard for causal inference in such demographic/statistical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data completeness and the 'unknown' category problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistics, however, are liable to another error; in most cases the religion of the suicide is not registered, and the column of the unknown always predominates over the others. It is sufficient to cite the Prussian statistics ... out of 5,673 registered suicides, quite 3,703 (65 per cent.) can give no answer to the question of the religion professed by the suicides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the quality of statistical evidence by checking registration completeness; large 'unknown' fractions (example: 65%) seriously weaken conclusions. Analysts should report and account for missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for race, social, occupational, and anthropological confounders
rubrics_metrics.description: This strong influence of race obliges one to proceed cautiously in attributing to the Mosaic religion the little tendency of Jews toward suicide... the influence of race... complica ted with that of religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses must consider race, social structure, urbanization, occupational distributions, consanguinity hypotheses, and other anthropological factors when attributing differences in suicide rates to religion; avoid simple causal claims without controlling for these covariates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of oversimplified minority/majority explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Legoyt reckons that 'the inclination toward suicide in the inhabitants belonging to any particular worship, in any given country, will diminish in direct ratio with their numerical inferiority' ... an attentive examination of facts does not altogether bear out Legoyt's conclusion; for we find that it is scarcely ever that minorities furnish the smallest contingent to the register of suicide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept theoretical claims (e.g., minorities have lower suicide rates due to moral coercion) without empirical validation; explore exceptions and local social dynamics rather than applying blanket rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum time-allocation recommendation for schools
rubrics_metrics.description: What we ask is that, say, six hours a week each should be devoted to mathematics, modern languages, and science, an arrangement which would still leave twenty hours for Latin and Greek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an educational standard/recommendation: allocate weekly hours to increase mathematics, modern languages, and science teaching (six hours each) while preserving classical instruction; this is proposed as a benchmark for 'more rational' school systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing measurement accuracy and interchangeability standard
rubrics_metrics.description: He devised a measuring apparatus, by which his workmen in making standard gauges are accustomed to take measurements to the .001 of an inch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce stringent measurement standards in workshops to achieve interchangeable parts and high precision manufacturing; explicit small-unit measurement (e.g., thousandths of an inch) is presented as a standard of excellence.
